### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **31** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class), org_membership_level (symbol, a field of const object APPROVER_TYPE_WORDS), org_membership_level (literal, a string literal in approvalApproverTypeOrgMembershipLevel))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via org_membership_level (symbol, a field of const object APPROVER_TYPE_WORDS), org_membership_level (literal, a string literal in approvalApproverTypeOrgMembershipLevel))_

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via org_membership_level (symbol, a field of const object APPROVER_TYPE_WORDS), org_membership_level (literal, a string literal in approvalApproverTypeOrgMembershipLevel))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via org_membership_level (symbol, a field of const object APPROVER_TYPE_WORDS), org_membership_level (literal, a string literal in approvalApproverTypeOrgMembershipLevel))_

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **250** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d8628ac7ab7b4a2dad8175e16800e687f6b3a201` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b266e42b3a97634565bc20f3e577c5ef10621a01` — the merge of head `59de666227c4f709934601cad8441b250aac4bce` into base `d8628ac7ab7b4a2dad8175e16800e687f6b3a201`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b266e42b3a97634565bc20f3e577c5ef10621a01 && git checkout b266e42b3a97634565bc20f3e577c5ef10621a01
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d8628ac7ab7b4a2dad8175e16800e687f6b3a201 59de666227c4f709934601cad8441b250aac4bce && git checkout -B drift-repro d8628ac7ab7b4a2dad8175e16800e687f6b3a201 && git merge --no-ff 59de666227c4f709934601cad8441b250aac4bce

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d8628ac7ab7b4a2dad8175e16800e687f6b3a201
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d8628ac7ab7b4a2dad8175e16800e687f6b3a201` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

L1 (L1-e) on head `59de666227`, card #36308: **ACCEPT**, with one landing condition (body only). No contract face is touched, so no L2 is owed.

**Landing condition.** The two residuals in the Acceptance notes (the multi-slot notice's English `who`, and the decide refusal staying an English sentence) are the unimplementable half of Done-when 2. `Fixes` stands only if they move to the card the seat files. Before landing, the two lines must name it as "carried by #N". With that, this PR delivers everything #36308 can deliver without a `service-messaging` nested-param shape or a REST `userMessage` channel, both outside this card's surface.

**Read**
- **Shape** (`l1-face.mjs --pr 36450`, CLEAN): open, draft, base `main`, `Fixes #36308`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The changeset is `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` patch. Gates at this head: 37 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed.
- **Done-when 1** (refusal and notice name a labelled position by its label in the reader's language; an unlabelled one keeps its name): met.
  - Both decide refusals (`excludeSubmitter` and the administrator override) compose the remedy with `notePositionLabels(slatePositions(pending), readerLabels(context))`, the one resolver the timeline uses. The card asked for no second resolver.
  - Pinned: a zh-CN decider reads `position '法务'`, ja-JP and no locale read `'Legal Counsel'`.
  - The remedy is composed only when it is said (`noOneElse`). A failed label read leaves the name standing, because `positionLabelSource` is wrapped.
  - The submitter notice: a one-slot slate rides `approvalNoApproverHoldingSlot` with `type` and `value` as keyed params (`{ key, fallback }`). That gives the recipient's pack label, then the declared label, then the name, rendered per recipient at delivery. It is pinned through the real `NotificationTextRenderer`: zh-CN `岗位「销售经理」`, no `position` or `sales_manager` left, ja-JP, en, and an unlabelled `treasury`.
- **Done-when 2** (no English type token for a zh-CN reader): met for the timeline note and the one-slot notice. The rest is under the landing condition above.
  - `approvalApproverTypePosition/Team/Department/OrgMembershipLevel`, `approvalNoApproverSlot`, `…SlotSeparator` and `…HoldingSlot` are present in all 11 packs.
  - The `en` type word is the machine token, so the stored English audit text is byte-identical ("Stored audit text stays as written").
- **Refactor.** `noApproverSentence` was split into `noApproverNotice` (notice params) and `noApproverNoteText` (rendered text). Absent `slots` and `who`, both still fall back to `approvalNoApprover`. A stored legacy `who` passes through as written.
- **Accepted, as stated.**
  - A legacy stored English `who` now renders without spaces in CJK, because the sentence lost its spaces for the type word. That is cosmetic, on old rows only.
  - The administrators' note keeps tokens for non-position types. It is outside this card's sentence.
- **Changeset, checked sentence by sentence.** It is true, including "A slate of several slots still sends one English `who`, with each position named by its declared label": `noApproverWho(note.slots, declaredLabel)` is called with no `render`.
- **Live run not owed.** The one boundary, per-recipient keyed rendering, is driven through the real `service-messaging` renderer.
